Mount Kosciuszko is the highest peak in Australia at seven thousand three hundred ten feet, located in the Great Dividing Range in New South Wales. Though modest in elevation compared to mountains on other continents, its gentle slopes and relative accessibility make it the easiest and most-climbed summit on the Seven Summits climbing list. Hundreds of thousands of visitors access it annually via hiking trails. The peak sits in the Snowy Mountains, part of the Great Dividing Range, a granite peak with sparse alpine vegetation. It is named after Polish military hero and American Revolutionary War officer Tadeusz Kosciuszko. Climbs are non-technical hikes accessible to children and non-climbers. The most popular route from Thredbo takes roughly three to four hours round-trip. The peak receives hundreds of thousands of visitors annually, making it among the world's most-summited mountains by raw numbers. Alpine ecology at the summit comprises grasses, low shrubs, and cushion plants adapted to extremes of wind and cold. Perpetual snow is rare at this elevation. For those pursuing the Seven Summits achievement, Mount Kosciuszko represents the easiest of the seven continental high points.
